paragraphs: latent embedding space (also known as “codebook”): $\boldsymbol{e}\in {R}^{K\times D}$
$K$ is the number of latent variable categories
$D$ is the embedding size. An individual embedding vector is ${\boldsymbol{e} }_{i}\in {R}^{D}$
Encoder $E(\boldsymbol{x})$ output  goes through a nearest-neighbor lookup to match to one of $K$ embedding vectors
matched code vector becomes the input for the decoder $D(\cdot )$

paragraphs: Structured Denoising Diffusion Models in Discrete State-Spaces
Traditional models only allow continuous data due to Gaussian Noise which can take on any real value, like pixel intensities in images
expands on discrete diffusion models by modelling structured discrete data in the noising process
discrete-appropriate noise is added: Could be flipping bits (classification), changing tokens (text) or changing between categorical states (categorization)

paragraphs: LLaDA is a masked diffusion model that follows standard pretraining and SFT while sampling via diffusion.
During pretraining, it masks all tokens randomly at ratio $t\sim U[0,1]$ ; in SFT, only response tokens may be masked.
The model simulates diffusion from full masking $(t=1)$ to unmasking $(t=0)$, predicting all masks simultaneously at each step with flexible remasking.
original_paragraphs: LLaDA is a masked diffusion model that follows standard pretraining and SFT while sampling via diffusion.
During pretraining, it masks all tokens randomly at ratio 𝑡∼𝑈[0,1] ; in SFT, only response tokens may be masked.
The model simulates diffusion from full masking (𝑡=1) to unmasking (𝑡=0), predicting all masks simultaneously at each step with flexible remasking.
